article.story: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Dave Canales is like most NFL coaches — he wants to keep his team's focus on the next game and avoid any potential outside distractions. But this past week was a little different for the Carolina Panthers. Canales spoke repeatedly to his players about the “championship opportunity” at hand, referring to the possibility of taking a commanding lead in the NFC South if everything fell right on Sunday with the other teams in the division. And they did for the Panthers. Bryce Young threw for 254 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and two more scores and the Panthers got a late defensive stop to beat Baltimore 35-33, sending the Ravens to their sixth straight loss. Carolina's victory, coupled with losses by Tampa Bay and New Orleans, gave the defending NFC South champion Panthers (5-5) a two-game lead in the division over the Buccaneers, Saints and Atlanta Falcons with seven games remaining in the regular season. It's the first time the Panthers have held a two-game lead in the NFC South since the end of the 2015 season — when they went to the Super Bowl. “Coach talked about it all week and we said it pregame: We can be fine with being good, but let's be great,” Hubbard said. “Why not us? Let's create some separation. This is a good opportunity in front of us and now we have to stack these wins.” Ryan Fitzgerald made a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left to give the Panthers the lead, marking the seventh lead change. But in a wild game that included two touchdowns off trick plays, an 86-yard kickoff return for a touchdown by Dontez Walker, two muffed punts and a safety, it seemed nothing was safe. The Panthers couldn't exhale until 33 seconds remained when Jacoby Brissett’s desperation heave down the right side sideline was broken up and deflected by Will Lee III and intercepted by his former Texas A&M teammate Tyrel Dodson. Lee, the team’s fourth-round draft pick, also forced two fumbles, including a strip of Justice Hill as the Ravens backup running back was approaching the goal line at the end of a nifty 36-yard run. The loose ball traveled out of the back of the end zone, resulting in a touchback. “It was just ball knowledge,” Lee said. “You see that stiff arm and you know he's not protecting the ball with the other arm. I just saw my shot. I was like, man, I got these long arms and I'm going to try to get a piece of the ball, and I did.” Canales later said it will go down as one of his favorite plays since he took over as the Panthers' coach in 2024. “It will be something that we point to — this is how we play football,” Canales said. “You never give up as long as you have a blade of grass and (the ball) is not across the goal line. Give it everything you got. It was just an unbelievable play." Hubbard took on a monster load again for the Panthers. One week after running for 92 yards on 27 carries and two touchdowns in a 20-17 win over the Saints, he carried the load with 27 more runs and helped wear down the Ravens. Hubbard joined Christian McCaffrey as the only Carolina players to get 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. It was another tough loss for the Ravens. Brissett finished 24 of 37 for 276 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Derrick Henry, who had a fumble early in the fourth quarter, scored on a 15-yard run with 6:32 left to give the Ravens (4-7) a 33-32 lead, but was taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion and did not return. Ravens coach Jesse Minter had no immediate update on Henry's status after the game. Henry finished with 13 carries for 94 yards, his second best total of the season. “They’re all tough. The last two weeks the team has battled their butts off and put the team in a position to have a chance to win. We haven’t gotten it done," Minter said. “We’re going to come in tomorrow and say, ‘It could’ve been this play or that play.’ It’s a one play at a time game and we didn’t get it done.” The Ravens hadn't scored more than 20 points in any of their last five games, but racked up 338 yards in the first half, including a 52-yard touchdown pass from Brissett to Rashod Bateman off a direct snap to Henry followed by two pitches in the backfield. The Panthers got two touchdown passes from Young and an 18-yard TD run from Hubbard to stay close before the break in what Minter called a “chaotic” first half. Injuries Ravens: Along with Henry's potential concussion, LB Trey Hendrickson left in the first half with a knee injury and OT Roger Rosengarten left in the second with a concussion. Panthers: CB Mike Jackson (groin) was active and played in his first game since Week 3. WR Jalen Coker left late in the fourth quarter with a concussion. Up next Ravens: at Houston on Sunday. Panthers: at Tampa Bay on Nov. 30. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
